newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Exxon units discuss downstream cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Japan Exxon units discuss downstream cooperation.

text.p: Three Japanese affiliates of U.S. Exxon Corp are in talks regarding refinery and storage sharing arrangements, company officials said on Monday.
But spokesmen from Japanese refiners General Sekiyu KK and Esso Sekiyu told Reuters that no deal had yet been finalised between themselves and the group's third party, Tonen Corp.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun, a financial daily, reported on Sunday that the firms will consolidate parts of their production sectors in the city of Kawasaki by early 1998.
"It's true we are considering (cooperative measures)...but it's not true that we've reached a decision on any of these matters at this moment," a General Sekiyu spokesman said.
He said that the companies were unlikely to take years to make a decision, but that he could not immediately say when they would reach a conclusion.
A spokeswoman from Esso Sekiyu said the company was also considering a proposal that would integrate sections of its lubricant oil production with fellow Exxon affiliate General Sekiyu.
"We are considering such an arrangement, but we have made no commitments," the spokeswoman said.
A third component of the agreement would involve the sharing of tanker and distribution infrastructure by the three companies.
Overall the firms stand to save some four billion yen, the newspaper report said.
Tonen officials were unavailable for comment.
Tonen Corp is the largest of the three companies in terms of capitalisation, followed by Esso Sekiyu and General Sekiyu.

Now in their second year of market deregulation and facing tighter budgets as a weaker yen versus the dollar boosts crude oil import costs, Japan's oil companies will face increasing pressure to streamline and economise on their downstream operations.
Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd and Showa Shell Sekiyu KK last February announced their intention to merge parts of their refinery and distribution systems.
